results.title: A  Hindu Cultural experience
results.text:
Pashupatinath is a biggest Hindu temple in the world. Even though the entrance to the temple is only for Hindus there is a lot that you can explore here. There are different ways to enter the area hence you might not see all of what the temple area has to offer depending on which route you enter. If this is you first visit I would suggest you enter through Gaushala (this is also where the main parking is). There are lots of shops here where you can buy antiques but be sure you bargain. 
If you are not a Hindu you cannot enter the main area but there is a path between the temple and parking which leads you to a place called "Aryaghat". This is just beside the river and cremations take place here. You  can walk on the other side of river towards a small hill . This place is very spiritual. Lot of benches are placed here under the trees, where you can sit, watch the cremations and see the temple. You can also see around 50 small temples here which are in built in same fashion. From this place you can start a small hike (30 mins ) or so into the temple forest. It is basically just staircases leading you deeper into the forest. Legend has it that this is where Lord Shiva lived. The walk is beautiful and you can see deers jumping around. The finishing of the hike is at another temple (guheswori) so make sure you know your way back .
Also in the evenings there is special ceremony beside the holy river where people chant mantras and they have lights and incense burning all over. This is just magical. The cremations may scare you off a little but if you want to know about Hindu culture and experince spirituality ... this is the place in kathmandu.
the only restroom around is in the main temple area (non hindus allowed) . there is no restroom on the 30 min staircase trek so use it before you start.  Also be careful of tourist guides here.....some of them are fake people just aiming at money.

results.title: An Experience in Itself
results.text:
This is one of the holiest Hindu shrines and is a marvel in itself. I have been there 4 years ago and things have certainly improved in the last 4 years.
There is the usual long queue to enter into the temple and you need to have at least 3-4 hours in hand for a good darshan of Lord Pashupatinath. This being a very old temple made of stone you have to keep in mind that it is a bit slippery in some places.
Western tourists would find the open air crematorium a curiousity !

results.title: The most holy temple for hindus Pashupati is a Hindu god, Also one of the eight avatars of Avalokitesh of Budhhists vara
results.text:
This temple is the most sacred temple for Hindus and for non -hindus it is place to see funeral rituals of Hindus.the temple is very beautiful with hundreds of statues, small temples of lord shiva and other hindu gods scattered within its premises. The main temple is also a masterpiece with beautiful carvings. The two storied golden roofs, silver doors on all four sides, five faced statue of lord shiva, two bronze bulls (one very big and other fourth of its size) in front of the western door etc makes this temple very beautiful. As photography is restricted the actual beauty of the temple area is not much known by the tourists. There is another very significant temple near it, the temple of Unmatta Bhairab. Unmatta Bhairav is supposed to be the fierce menifestation of lord shiva. The idol of Unmatta Bhairav in the most stark nudity exposing the pro-creative organ in its most prominent form. this god is believed to protect the children, also who can not conceive for a long time comes to worship this god. There are such several marvellous idols. When climb down at the bank of Bagmati where cremation goes on, one can see a small but very important statue of KALKI or Kali (not goddess Kaali). This statue is half buried into the ground. This statue is said to be built during Kiratas period (fifteen hundred years ago) and believed that if this comes out fully the earth will be destroyed and new origin starts again. 
In the evening one can see special arti a(worshiping with lights and hymns) t the bank of Bagmati. I think guides should tell this to the tourists also besides death rituals. They can see the temple of kali (or Birupaksha) ..to see the statue I think they may need a normal binocular........ If possible good to try evening visit to see the Arti......

P.S. Free entrance for Hindus while NPR 500 for non-Hindus
